newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai foreign bank assets up 50 pct by end-96.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai foreign bank assets up 50 pct by end-96.

text.p: Branches of foreign banks and other financial institutions in Shanghai had $13.5 billion in assets by the end of 1996, a rise of 50 percent against the end of 1995, a report by the People's Bank of China said on Friday.

The report by the Shanghai branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, said the branch's assets accounted for 45 percent of the assets all foreign financial institutions had in China, it said.

In 1996, overseas financial institutions in Shanghai had combined profits of $52.44 million, an increase of 42 percent against the previous year, comprising 29 percent of the total in China, the report said.

According to the bank's figures, the Shanghai branch of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank was the biggest in terms of total assets, foreign currency loans and foreign currency deposits, while Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp was tops in terms of export settlements.
By the end of 1996, the central bank branch had approved 46 foreign banks, accounting firms and insurance companies to open branches with 41 in operation, it said.
Japan had the largest number, with 11 banks and one insurance company, followed by France, the United States, South Korea, Germany and Britain, it said.
A total of 147 other foreign financial institutions had opened representative offices in Shanghai by the end of 1996, the report said.
